title: Interleaved queue + credit-bridge for tiered routing with regional fallback variants
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: During region-level capacity pressure and quota exhaustion we observe two failure modes: (1) paid customers experience accidental throughput loss when conservative admission rejects their requests to preserve free-tier tokens; (2) free requests overwhelm cheap-model fallbacks causing elevated latencies that impact SLOs for all tiers. We need a unified admission strategy that preserves enterprise SLAs, fairly preserves paid customers' reserved credits, and gracefully degrades free traffic to lower-cost model variants and regional backups.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Enterprise requests maintain target p95 <= 150ms under simulated mixed load where total token consumption is 3x provisioned.
2) Paid-tier request success rate stays >= 99.5% for traffic with available credit > 20% of monthly allocation.
3) When a region is capacity-constrained, at least 95% of routed paid+enterprise traffic is spilled to compatible regional model variants within 200ms routing decision latency.
4) Free-tier traffic is automatically downgraded to configured fallback model variants (smaller/quantized) with documented cost reduction, and documented impact on output quality in canary prompts.
5) Implement feature flag to enable/disable credit-bridge behavior and interleaving per-customer.
6) End-to-end tests and chaos tests included in CI that simulate quota exhaustion and regional outage.
design_notes:
Proposal overview: implement an Interleaved Admission Controller (IAC) sitting between the API gateway and routing engine. IAC components:
- Tiered logical queues: enterprise, paid, free. Each queue has dynamic admission thresholds driven by token budgets and latency headroom.
- Credit-bridge window: when a paid tenant is temporarily over its short-term burst quota but has long-term credit remaining, allow a bounded 'borrow' of tokens from reserved credit with a decaying repayment schedule to avoid immediate denial.
- Soft preemption: enterprise requests can preempt lower-priority queued items but we cap preemptions per-second to avoid starvation.
- Regional spillback rules: if region X lacks capacity for a model variant, IAC consults model-compatibility matrix to spill to nearest region with matching quantization/sequence length support and applies per-tenant routing policy (pin-to-region or allow-spill).
- Fallback model variants: define fallback mapping: free -> tiny-quantized, paid -> small-quantized (if needed), enterprise -> full-precision (no fallback except as last resort).
- Observability hooks: emit per-decision events (reason, tokens_charged, credit_borrowed, spill_region, fallback_used) and tag by tenant and route for downstream dashboards.
Trade-offs considered:
- Complexity vs fairness: credit-bridge adds bookkeeping and race conditions across distributed admission controllers; we limit scope to a 2s local borrowing window with eventual sync to central quota ledger to reduce consistency pressure.
- Cost vs latency: spilling to remote region may increase latency; prioritized enterprise traffic can accept cross-region latency up to a configured SLA.
- Quality vs cost for free tier: fallback mapping exposes quality regressions; we require a small eval set per tenant to track regression and a quick rollback path.
Alternative considered: pessimistic rejection (current) or token-lottery admission. Rejected due to poor UX for paid customers and unpredictable latencies respectively.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): implement IAC in a single control-plane region and enable for 5 internal tenants + 3 seeded external paid tenants. Run canary for 2 weeks with feature flag off for rest of traffic.
Phase 2 (gradual): enable credit-bridge for all paid tenants with monitoring thresholds; promote IAC to two additional regions.
Phase 3 (global): enable for free tier fallback with conservative downgrade rules and automated rollback on regression alerts.
Rollback: feature flag kill-switch and per-region kill flagged routing to bypass IAC and return to legacy admission.
Telemetry gating: must hit metrics targets for 48h before proceeding from Phase 1 to 2.
test_plan:
Unit tests for admission logic and credit accounting. Integration tests: simulate mixed-tier traffic bursts with synthetic clients and validate routing decisions and token debits against central ledger. Chaos tests: kill regional model nodes and ensure spillback routes and fallbacks exercise correctly. Performance tests: measure decision latency under 10k RPS and ensure per-decision latency < 5ms median.
Canary validation: run canary workload with observed p50/p95/p99, error rates, and credit-recovery histograms. Include a short prompt-based eval to validate fallback model outputs against golden set.
metrics:
- decision_latency_ms (median,p95,p99)
- credit_borrowed_tokens_per_tenant
- spillback_rate_by_region
- fallback_usage_rate_by_tier
- paid_success_rate
- enterprise_preemptions_per_minute
- observed_quality_regression_rate_on_fallback_prompts
comments: 2026-02-26 - Initial design draft posted. Asked SRE to validate cost model for cross-region spillback. (Asha)
2026-03-02 - Feedback from Product: require per-tenant opt-out for cross-region spill because some customers cannot allow cross-border routing. Added pin-to-region flag to design. (Nora Kim)

2026-03-05 - Engineering review: raised concern about race between local borrow and central ledger reconciliation. Decided on 2s local borrow window and async reconcile job with compensating debit. (Daniel)
2026-03-09 - Design review: UX approved fallback mapping and requested small test suite for subjective output quality. (María González)
2026-03-12 - Implementation: core admission loop implemented, local unit tests green. Opening PR for IAC infra and canary config. Next: integrate observability events and run canary. (Daniel)
